selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The CATFISH Act of 2026 establishes stricter criminal penalties for romance scams targeting individuals aged 60 and older. It requires financial institutions and large retailers to implement fraud-prevention training, mandates that financial institutions report specific suspicious activities involving senior customers to the Treasury Department, and orders studies and guidance on victim remedies and prevention methods.

affected_groups.effect: Receive enhanced legal protections against romance fraud, potential interventions by retailers when purchasing large gift cards, and increased fraud monitoring and reporting by financial institutions.
Must implement internal controls, staff training, customer education, and mandatory reporting procedures for suspicious account activities, or face civil penalties of up to $50,000 per violation.
affected_groups.group: Covered financial institutions and digital asset providers

affected_groups.effect: Must train employees to intervene, provide advisories, and assist senior customers with calling the National Elder Fraud Hotline when purchasing gift cards valued over $500.
affected_groups.group: Covered retailers with 500 or more employees

affected_groups.effect: Face harsher criminal penalties, including up to 10 additional years in prison and fines up to $1,000,000.
affected_groups.group: Perpetrators of romance fraud targeting seniors

key_provisions: Adds up to 10 additional years of imprisonment and fines of up to $1,000,000 for convictions of mail fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, or related offenses committed in furtherance of romance fraud targeting individuals aged 60 or older.

Requires the FBI to develop training programs for financial institutions on identifying and preventing romance fraud, and for large retailers to train employees to intervene when senior customers purchase gift cards valued over $500.

Mandates that covered financial institutions report specified suspicious activities regarding senior customer accounts to the Secretary of the Treasury, along with detailed transaction records and documentation.
Requires financial institutions to establish enhanced internal controls, provide employee training, give instructions to seniors on reporting fraud, and share information on trending frauds.

Authorizes covered banking agencies to bring civil actions for penalties up to $50,000 for each violation of the financial institution requirements, with a safe harbor for institutions acting in good faith under compliant procedures.
Directs the Comptroller General to study existing romance fraud remedies, potential expansions to the Crime Victims Fund, and options for new support programs.
Requires the Treasury Secretary to issue rules establishing minimum compliance standards and guidance on best practices, including transaction holds and disbursement delays.
missing_information: The exact timeline for when financial institutions must have their internal controls fully operational, other than the civil penalty effective date being one year after enactment.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The CATFISH Act of 2026 establishes stricter criminal penalties for romance scams targeting individuals aged 60 and older. It requires financial institutions and large retailers to implement fraud-prevention training, mandates that financial institutions report specific suspicious activities involving senior customers to the Treasury Department, and orders studies and guidance on victim remedies and prevention methods.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a comprehensive federal framework aimed at curbing romance and confidence scams targeting older Americans. By combining tougher criminal sentences for offenders with regulatory mandates for financial institutions and large retailers to detect, report, and disrupt suspected elder fraud, the legislation targets the financial pipelines used in these schemes. The significance score reflects a moderate-to-substantial policy change for financial compliance and retail gift card sales, balanced against targeted criminal enforcement.
